To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the predictive coding/biested competition (PC/ BC) model of V1 provides an account of the response of cells in V1 to simple visual stimuli, and that this model also provides an account of visual salience in the context of visual search.
the predictive coding/biested competition (PC/RC) model of V1 can successfully simulate the saliency effects of unique items, contours and borders.

the biased competition model of visual attention can explain the psychophysical data relating the saliency map to visual search and contour integration, but only if the model is extended to include the prediction of visual input by a hierarchy of cortical modules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the computational and neural mechanisms that underlie the visual system's ability to detect and respond to salient stimuli.
the role of predictive coding in the visual system.
the computational and neural mechanisms of visual saliency and their relation to attention, and with the neural mechanisms of visual awareness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PC/BC can provide a unified account of both the psychophysics of salience and the response properties of V1 neurons.
PC/BC provides the first successful model of the V2 hypothesis of visual salience.
PC/BC provides a unified account of the response profiles of orientation tuned V1 cells and a variety of psychophysical measures of salience.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the predictive coding/biases competition model is a good model for the V1 salience map.

the PC/BC model provides a detailed account of V1 response properties, and also provides a possible implementation for the V1 salience map hypothesis, which in turn can be interpreted as a predictive coding mechanism for the control of attention.
the saliency map is the result of the interaction between bottom-up and top-down processes, and that this interaction is mediated by the activity of orientation tuned cells within V1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
saliency is an emergent phenomenon of predictive coding and is not a separate mechanism.
the PC/BC model provides a unified account of a diverse set of visual phenomena, including visual salience.

predictive coding can account for a variety of salience effects in visual perception, and that the same model may be able to account for salience effects in other domains, such as audition, touch and olfaction.
